title: Smarter call-graph orchestration, fallback plumbing, and loop-sanity harness
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Design and implement a robust orchestration layer for multi-tool/function call graphs that ensures safe result injection, streaming-friendly responses, and compatibility across API client versions. Deliverables: 1) call-graph executor with depth and fanout controls, 2) result plumbing rules (explicit injection vs. reference-only), 3) loop and recursion detector with circuit-breaker semantics, 4) streaming-friendly partial result semantics and backpressure handling, and 5) compatibility shim for older SDKs. Acceptance criteria: prevents unbounded recursion in >99.9% of real traces, produces deterministic structured outputs under retries, supports streaming of intermediate tool outputs without leaking internal state, and includes telemetry for recursion events and fallback triggers.
notes: This work touches runtime executor, streaming layer, and SDK compatibility. We will feature-flag the runtime changes and gate the compatibility shim behind client version negotiation. Plan calls for a staged rollout: internal canary -> dedicated pools -> hosted default. Consideration: result plumbing must balance safety (no unintended injection of tool outputs into model prompts) with ergonomics (structured results should be accessible to caller code).
comments: 2026-03-02 — Spike completed: instrumented a lightweight call-graph tracer in a dev branch and replayed 1k real requests; observed two pathological loops (mutually recursive tool calls) in a chatbot integration. Recorded traces and stack samples in Grafana.

2026-03-04 — Design review with PM and Design: agreed on explicit injection markers ("inject:true") in tool metadata for any result permitted to be reinjected into the LM prompt; default = inject:false. Design asked for a compatibility path for SDKs that predate inject flag.

2026-03-05 — Engineering sync: decided on three layered protections: 1) static graph depth/fanout limits (configurable per-project), 2) dynamic recursion detector using call digest and TTLed per-session fingerprinting, 3) circuit-breaker that converts further tool calls to noop stubs returning safe structured placeholders. Trade-off: stubbing can reduce fidelity but prevents availability regressions.

2026-03-06 — PR #2184 created with initial call-graph executor and unit tests for depth limits. Tests include streaming path verification (partial outputs emit with a stub marker) and idempotency token propagation for retried tool calls.

2026-03-07 — Feedback from reliability: add an opt-in telemetry field on tool responses to indicate whether response was used for injection; this allows post-hoc audits and quality regressions tied to injection policy changes.

2026-03-08 — Implemented compatibility shim: if client version < 2.4.0, runtime treats all tool outputs as reference-only unless explicit client sets legacy_inject=true. Security flagged this as high-risk; we added an audit log entry for legacy_inject usage.

2026-03-09 — Benchmarks: microbench shows median latency regression of +3.2ms for short chains (<=3 calls) and tail improvement under load due to early stubbing preventing exponential fanout. Documented results in attachment links.

2026-03-10 — Next steps: finish integration tests for streaming backpressure (verify no internal state leakage when client disconnects), add end-to-end demo app for SEs, and schedule canary rollout to internal cluster on 2026-03-15. Assign follow-ups: ENG-76422 implement sandboxed idempotency store, ENG-76423 telemetry enrichment and alerts, ENG-76424 SDK compatibility doc and client test harness.
